findings.title: HC rules still name removed commands
findings.detail:
B71 (story.md:314): 'every rule that names an old command (O1, O2, O5, MO5, S7, BS9, GR7, K2a, HC4–HC13, …) to name the new one'. AC3 repeats it. The HC rules live in .agents/SPEC-herdr-cockpit.md, and PRD O1 still points at 'SPEC-herdr-cockpit HC4–HC8'. That file's key table (lines 52–57) still maps keys to `norn answer <unit>`, `norn approve <unit>`, `norn approve <unit> --reject`, `norn take`, `norn unstick` and `norn trace`. The diff does not touch the file. Other .agents/SPEC-*.md files and LIMITATIONS.md also still name old commands (SPEC-cockpit ~23 lines, SPEC-base-sync-and-qa ~14, SPEC-auto-mode-recovery ~3, LIMITATIONS ~6). AC3 does not cite those rules by id.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Rename the commands in the HC rules of SPEC-herdr-cockpit.md to the new surface (story answer/approve/reject, run rerun/view, …), and add the file to the lint's scanned files. Decide whether the other SPEC-*.md files and LIMITATIONS.md are amended or explicitly exempted as history.

findings.title: PRD S9 still names the removed `take` command
findings.detail:
S9 reads '`brief` includes it; `take` prints it.' `take` is in REMOVED_COMMANDS (B71). The lint misses it because the line has no `norn ` prefix.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Name the command that now prints the handoff (e.g. `norn story start` / `run view`, whichever replaced take's printing). Grep the PRD for bare backticked removed verbs (`take`, `unstick`, `drop`, `trace`, `why`, `inbox`, `cockpit`) and keep only the receipt-kind uses (B70).

findings.title: Shipped config template still says `norn open`
findings.detail:
Line 48 reads 'manual (you, with norn open)'. `open` is a removed command (B5), and AC1/B8 say nothing shipped may name one. The slice edited line 49, right below it. The lint misses it because it is an unquoted comment.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Change it to 'with `norn story start`' or equivalent.

findings.title: Lint checks only quoted text in docs and .ts, so prose gets through
findings.detail:
oldCommandHits checks only backtick, single-quote and double-quote spans outside .sh/.toml. Unquoted prose, .ts comments and fenced code blocks are not checked. F2 and F3 got through this way. AC1 says the lint 'fails when any … names a removed command'.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Scan whole lines in fenced blocks and comments as well. Consider also matching bare `norn <old>` in prose, using the existing allowlist for legitimate phrases (e.g. 'a norn workflow'), or document the narrowing in the slice.

findings.title: Lint passes vacuously if REMOVED_COMMANDS cannot be read
findings.detail:
The `?.[1] ?? "[]"` fallback is a silent catch. If the one-line regex stops matching commands.ts (the line is wrapped, the constant renamed or moved), REMOVED_COMMANDS becomes [] and OLD_COMMAND becomes `(?:\bnorn|"\$NORN")\s+()(?![\w-])`. That pattern can never satisfy the lookahead in practice, so every file passes and the lint guards nothing.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Drop the fallback and fail loudly, e.g. `expect(REMOVED_COMMANDS.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)` or throw when the regex does not match.

findings.title: next.sh branches on refusal prose, not the refusal code (P8)
findings.detail:
The `case` matches the literal error text 'No agent waits for you'. AGENTS.md (Decisions, P8): 'code branches on the exit code and --json data, never on markdown'/prose. The refusal from run attach carries a `code` (nothing_to_attach, run-attach.ts). Rewording the message silently changes which toast shows. The sed extraction also truncates an error or do_instead value at the first escaped quote.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Extract `code` (reuse one JSON-field helper alongside ctx_get in lib.sh instead of a second hand-rolled sed) and branch on `nothing_to_attach`.

findings.title: open.sh behaviour depends on untested Herdr environment assumptions
findings.detail:
The old action passed --target-pane <focused_pane_id> (HC9) and ran "$NORN" (NORN_BIN, then PATH, then the shim). The new one relies on `status --watch --pane`: (a) it refuses not_in_herdr unless HERDR_ENV or HERDR_SOCKET_PATH is in the action's environment (runtime/cockpit.ts:29); (b) without HERDR_PANE_ID it splits with no --current, so it may not land below the focused pane; (c) the split pane runs the literal `norn status --watch` (core commands.ts:71), not $NORN, so it fails when norn is not on PATH even though the action reports success. The implementer flagged (b).
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Check (a)–(c) in real Herdr during AC4 QA. If they fail, pass the focused pane and the norn binary through to the split.

findings.title: NORN_COCKPIT_DIR naming survives the cockpit command removal
findings.detail:
pick.sh:4 and pick-open.sh:3 still use NORN_COCKPIT_DIR. 'cockpit' remains the name of the view, so this is harmless.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Leave it, or rename it if 'cockpit' is meant to go away entirely.
